text:
Erik Cernak is the kind of defenseman whose best nights barely show on the scoresheet, which makes his recent run of assists a surprise. He has seven points in his last ten games, all assists, against about three we'd expect at his ice time. He still has no goals in 19 games.

Our form check calls it partly real. The chances with him on the ice are up only a little (8.4 on-ice expected goals, the quality of chances, against 8.1 usual), so his teammates' finishing is doing most of the work. The underlying play is still good: at five on five Tampa Bay takes 62.8% of the expected goals with him on, 7.6 points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him taking chances away last season (86th percentile), though penalties cost him 2.5 goals.

He missed games in mid-November, out alongside Anthony Cirelli, and was back on Nov. 17. Two nights later he played 22 minutes against Edmonton. The 6'4" two-time Stanley Cup winner's job is hits (32), blocks (30) and penalty killing, and Tampa clearly still leans on him for it.
headline: Erik Cernak is setting up goals now
